# TorqueSpec

> Bolt torque specification database. Calculated from ISO 898-1, SAE J429, and VDI 2230 standards using T = K × D × F.

## Main Pages

- [Homepage](https://torquespec.org/): Search all bolt torque specifications
- [Metric Bolts](https://torquespec.org/metric/): ISO metric bolt torque chart — M3 to M64, classes 4.6–12.9
- [Imperial Bolts](https://torquespec.org/imperial/): SAE imperial bolt torque chart — #6 to 1-1/2", grades 2, 5, 8
- [Lug Nut Torque by Vehicle](https://torquespec.org/lug-nuts/): Wheel torque, bolt pattern, thread and socket for 102 models
- [Component Torque Specs](https://torquespec.org/torque/): Oil drain plug, spark plug, head bolt, valve cover, axle nut, caliper, flywheel, rocker arm
- [Torque Calculator](https://torquespec.org/calculator/): Interactive bolt torque calculator with all unit conversions
- [About / Methodology](https://torquespec.org/about/): How we calculate — formula, standards, K-factor table, validation

## Component Torque Specs

- [Spark Plug Torque](https://torquespec.org/torque/spark-plug/): By thread size and seat type; 14 mm gasket seat 18–26 ft·lbs
- [Head Bolt Torque](https://torquespec.org/torque/head-bolt/): Staged sequences and torque-to-yield bolts explained
- [Valve Cover Bolt Torque](https://torquespec.org/torque/valve-cover/): 60–106 in·lbs by engine family
- [Axle Nut Torque](https://torquespec.org/torque/axle-nut/): 130–230 ft·lbs by manufacturer; staked and stretch nuts
- [Brake Caliper Bolt Torque](https://torquespec.org/torque/caliper-bolt/): Guide pins 20–31 ft·lbs, brackets 70–130 ft·lbs
- [Flywheel Bolt Torque](https://torquespec.org/torque/flywheel/): 45–85 ft·lbs by engine family
- [Rocker Arm Torque](https://torquespec.org/torque/rocker-arm/): 15–25 ft·lbs; shaft, pedestal and adjustable designs

## Unit Converters

- [Nm to Ft Lbs](https://torquespec.org/convert/nm-to-ft-lbs/): ft·lbs = N·m × 0.7375621; 100 N·m = 73.8 ft·lbs
- [Inch Pounds to Foot Pounds](https://torquespec.org/convert/inch-pounds-to-foot-pounds/): ft·lbs = in·lbs ÷ 12; 100 in·lbs = 8.33 ft·lbs
- [Ft Lbs to Nm](https://torquespec.org/convert/ft-lbs-to-nm/): N·m = ft·lbs × 1.3558179
- [Nm to In Lbs](https://torquespec.org/convert/nm-to-in-lbs/): in·lbs = N·m × 8.8507458

## Data Coverage

- **Metric:** 25 sizes (M3–M64) × 9 property classes (4.6, 4.8, 5.6, 5.8, 6.8, 8.8, 9.8, 10.9, 12.9) = 210 combinations
- **Imperial:** 17 sizes (#6–1-1/2") × 3 grades (2, 5, 8) = 51 combinations
- **Surface conditions:** 6 per combination (dry K=0.20, oiled K=0.15, zinc plated K=0.18, waxed K=0.10, MoS₂ K=0.12, galvanized K=0.25)
- **Thread types:** Coarse + fine (metric), UNC + UNF (imperial)
- **Units:** N·m, ft·lbs, in·lbs, kgf·cm
- **Vehicle lug nuts:** 102 models across 19 makes — torque, bolt pattern, thread size, socket, lug count and generation history
- **Components:** 8 component torque pages (oil drain plug, spark plug, head bolt, valve cover, axle nut, caliper bolt, flywheel, rocker arm)

## Methodology

Bolt size-and-grade torque values are calculated, not copied. Formula: T = K × D × F, where F = 0.75 × proof_stress × stress_area. Proof stress from ISO 898-1 (metric) and SAE J429 (imperial). Stress areas from ISO 261/262 and ASME B1.1. K-factors from VDI 2230. Cross-referenced against Portland Bolt, Fastenal, Bolt Depot and Fractory reference tables. Where a source shares our 75%-of-proof preload basis and K-factor, agreement is within about 2%; Fractory’s metric tables use a different preload basis, so their absolute values sit on a different footing and are used to check ratios rather than absolute numbers. Proof stress is applied per diameter tier (Class 8.8: 580 MPa ≤M16, 600 MPa M18+; SAE Grade 2 and Grade 5 step down above their threshold diameters).

Vehicle lug nut and component torque pages are different in kind: those figures are manufacturer specifications, not outputs of T = K × D × F. Real wheel, spark plug and oil pan joints are limited by the softer component or a sealing element rather than by the bolt, so the general formula does not apply. Each vehicle page names the generation and year range its figure covers and lists earlier generations where the pattern, thread or torque changed.
